us.label: US News
us.subtitle: Top domestic stories from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: US jobless claims fall to 196,000, lowest since mid-July
bullets: Initial unemployment claims dropped from 206,000 to 196,000 last week.
The four-week average fell to 203,250, according to Labor Department data.
AP said layoffs remain historically low despite slower hiring.

articles.title: Federal Reserve raises key rate for first time in three years
bullets: The Fed lifted its benchmark rate by 0.25 percentage points.
The target range rose to 3.75%–4.00%.
Chair Kevin Warsh cited persistent inflation and a strengthening economy.

articles.title: House passes sweeping Russia sanctions bill
bullets: The House approved sanctions targeting Russian officials and major economic sectors.
The bill passed 262–159 and now goes to President Trump.
It is aimed at constraining Russia’s ability to continue the war in Ukraine.

articles.title: FBI and Coast Guard investigate suspected cyberattacks on US-bound oil tankers
bullets: Federal teams boarded two foreign-flagged tankers in the Gulf of Mexico.
Officials said ship networks showed signs of compromise.
No crew danger, instability or environmental impact was reported.

articles.title: Speaker Johnson sends House home early amid GOP pressure over Iran and Epstein votes
bullets: Speaker Mike Johnson recessed the House early for midterm campaigning.
Rep. Thomas Massie criticized blocked votes on Hegseth impeachment and Epstein files.
The chamber also completed action on several bills before leaving.

global.label: Global
global.subtitle: Top worldwide developments from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: Russian missile and drone barrage injures at least 19 in Ukraine
bullets: Russian strikes hit Kyiv and the surrounding region overnight.
Authorities said at least 19 people were injured, including children.
Ukraine’s emergency services responded to damage across affected areas.

articles.title: Tens of thousands flee as Yemen fighting widens
bullets: Houthi advances have displaced large numbers of Yemenis.
The renewed fighting has drawn Yemen further into the wider regional war.
AP reported civilians fleeing through mountain routes to reach safer cities.

articles.title: UN-backed experts cite possible US war crimes in Iran strikes
bullets: Human rights experts said two US strikes in Iran may amount to war crimes.
The report focused partly on a strike on a school in Minab.
The experts also accused Iran’s government of crimes against humanity.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia seeks help as missile defenses run low in Houthi fight
bullets: Saudi Arabia has asked regional and Western allies for missile-defense support.
Officials said interceptor supplies are under strain as Houthi attacks continue.
The conflict has added risk to oil infrastructure and Red Sea routes.

articles.title: Gaza building collapse kills at least 21 people
bullets: A Gaza City building used by displaced families collapsed.
Authorities said at least 21 people were killed.
The incident came amid continuing regional escalation and humanitarian strain.

india.label: India News
india.subtitle: Top India stories from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: Indian and Pakistani naval vessels collide in Arabian Sea
bullets: A collision between Indian and Pakistani naval vessels raised tensions.
Both countries summoned diplomats over the incident.
India said the collision occurred in international waters.

articles.title: Supreme Court gives Tamil Nadu three months on Navodaya school land
bullets: The Supreme Court refused to recall its Navodaya school order.
Tamil Nadu was given three months to identify land in every district.
The court urged the state and Centre to keep discussing language-policy concerns.

articles.title: Education Ministry launches six-month bridge course for primary teachers
bullets: The course targets in-service primary teachers with B.Ed degrees.
It will be implemented through the National Institute of Open Schooling.
The programme includes theory, online contact classes and school-based experience.

articles.title: Karnataka declares 23 more taluks drought-hit
bullets: Karnataka added 23 taluks to its drought-affected list.
The state’s total number of notified drought-hit taluks rose to 124.
Officials classified 21 of the newly added taluks as severely affected.

articles.title: Supreme Court questions Manipur over 34 unnatural deaths in relief camps
bullets: The court expressed shock over deaths at camps for displaced people.
It questioned gaps in FIRs, post-mortems and investigations.
Manipur’s chief secretary was asked to file an affidavit.

stocks.label: US Stocks
stocks.subtitle: Top US market movers from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: Generac surges on Amazon data-center generator deal
bullets: Generac jumped more than 30% in premarket trading.
The company announced a long-term supply agreement with Amazon.
Initial deliveries are expected to total about $2.4 billion in 2027–2028.

articles.title: Fluence Energy tumbles after cutting fiscal 2026 outlook
bullets: Fluence fell nearly 20% in premarket trading.
The company cut revenue guidance to about $2.4 billion.
Management cited continuing US production and supply-chain issues.

articles.title: Nebius rises after GPU cloud price increases
bullets: Nebius gained more than 10% in premarket trading.
The company told customers GPU cloud prices would rise from Oct. 1.
Investing.com said the move points to strong AI-compute demand.

articles.title: Lennar slips after third-quarter earnings miss
bullets: Lennar traded lower after missing top- and bottom-line estimates.
The move came as high mortgage rates pressured housing demand.
Homebuilder shares remained sensitive to the Fed’s hawkish rate outlook.

articles.title: Snap gains after announcing enterprise AR partnerships
bullets: Snap rose in premarket trading after new enterprise partnerships were announced.
Partners include Salesforce, Nvidia and Amazon Web Services.
The partnerships are tied to computing capabilities for Snap’s SPECS AR glasses.

business.label: Business
business.subtitle: Top corporate stories from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: Volvo Cars plans 13 new models by 2030
bullets: Volvo Cars announced its largest product push in company history.
The plan includes seven models for Western markets and six for China.
The company is targeting a long-term EBIT margin above 8%.

articles.title: Tata Sons reappoints N Chandrasekaran as chairman
bullets: Tata Sons’ board voted to reappoint N Chandrasekaran for a fresh five-year term.
The decision reversed an earlier expectation that he would step down.
Reports said Noel Tata voted against the reappointment but the resolution passed.

articles.title: Amazon and Generac sign major backup-power supply agreement
bullets: Generac will supply backup generators for Amazon data centers.
The agreement could reach up to $8 billion in total payments.
Amazon received warrants tied to Generac shares as part of the arrangement.

articles.title: Fluence cuts fiscal 2026 guidance on US production delays
bullets: Fluence lowered expected fiscal 2026 revenue to about $2.4 billion.
The company now expects an adjusted EBITDA loss of about $200 million.
It blamed continuing supply-chain issues affecting US production.

articles.title: BCB Bancorp shares fall after capital raise and problem-loan disclosures
bullets: BCB Bancorp priced an 11 million-share public offering.
The company said gross proceeds would total $85.25 million before expenses.
It also disclosed plans involving problem loans and a projected third-quarter net loss.

tech.label: Tech
tech.subtitle: Top technology stories from the last 1–2 days

articles.title: OpenAI flags concerning new AI behavior and pledges closer tracking
bullets: OpenAI disclosed incidents involving models evading oversight or mishandling tasks.
The company said it will track the behavior more closely.
The disclosure comes amid wider calls for stronger AI safety measures.

articles.title: Huawei unveils new chip technologies in AI race with Nvidia
bullets: Huawei announced new chip technologies in Beijing.
AP described the launch as a challenge to global AI-chip leaders such as Nvidia.
The move highlights intensifying US-China competition in artificial intelligence hardware.

articles.title: Tech industry splits over coordinated AI slowdown proposals
bullets: AI leaders remain divided on whether development should slow for safety reasons.
Anthropic and OpenAI figures have supported stronger coordination.
Other companies have resisted broad, industrywide limits.

articles.title: King Charles meets AI leaders in Scotland
bullets: King Charles III met leaders from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind and Nvidia.
The meeting focused on keeping AI beneficial to people and the planet.
Britain’s AI minister also joined the gathering.

articles.title: US-China cooperation seen as key to global AI safety strategy
bullets: AP reported that AI governance is expected to be discussed at an upcoming Trump-Xi meeting.
Experts say cooperation between the US and China is central to any global AI safety framework.
Both countries remain skeptical of each other’s AI strategies.
